cases.blind_review_reason: Five declared voice outcomes each compared by Welch t-test at unadjusted alpha = 0.05, with two significance claims. Script and report state no multiple-comparison adjustment was applied.
Four declared juice-quality outcomes each compared by two-sample t-test and judged at unadjusted alpha = 0.05, with three significance claims. Script and report state no adjustment is applied.

Six declared outcomes each tested at unadjusted alpha = 0.05, yielding three significance claims including a borderline p = 0.047. The methods appendix states no multiple-comparison adjustment was applied.

Three declared scorpion outcomes each tested by Welch t-test and judged at unadjusted alpha = 0.05, with two significance claims. Script and report state no multiple-comparison adjustment of any kind was applied.

Partial correction. Holm covers only the two primary outcomes; the other five declared outcomes get unadjusted per-outcome significance verdicts at 0.05, and three are declared to differ on that basis.

Partial correction. Only the two prescribing-relevant outcomes have p-values multiplied by five; the remaining three declared outcomes receive unadjusted per-outcome verdicts at 0.05, as the report admits.

All five declared outcomes passed in one call to statsmodels multipletests, whose default Holm-Sidak method controls family-wise error. Verdicts come only from adjusted p-values; reported adjusted values match that method.
Sidak per-comparison threshold computed in code from the family size: 1 - 0.95^(1/4) = 0.012741. All four declared outcomes judged against it, not against 0.05. Arithmetic checks out.
All five declared outcomes adjusted together by the Holm step-down procedure via pingouin.multicomp at family-wise alpha = 0.05. Every verdict is read from adjusted p-values, none from raw ones.

Hand-coded Holm-Bonferroni across all four declared outcomes with correct arithmetic and monotonicity; verdicts from adjusted p-values. The step-count sensitivity re-run is explicitly non-inferential and carries no verdict.
Pre-fixed discovery/validation split. Screening in the discovery half makes no claims; all confirmatory conclusions come from the validation half at a Bonferroni level of 0.05/3 = 0.0167.
The stage-one gate is an effect-size sum against an arbitrary cut-off, not a level-alpha test, and uses the same carcasses. Four per-outcome verdicts then run unadjusted at 0.05.

Correction performed upstream: all five declared outcomes adjusted together as one family (Holm), and every verdict read from the adjusted p-value at the 5 percent family-wise level. Raw p-values carry no verdict.

Family-wide control by max-statistic label permutation: 5000 shuffles, each contributing the largest absolute Welch t across all five outcomes. Every outcome judged against that single family-maximum distribution.
Pre-registered corrected threshold: the protocol fixed alpha = 0.01 as 0.05 divided by the family of five before enrolment. Arithmetic is valid and all five outcomes are judged against it.
